messages:
alex: heads-up — walrus deploy to eu-west failed during env injection, canary never came up. seeing SOPS decrypt errors in the gitops job :facepalm:

maria: on it. which job? the `ci/gitops/apply-walrus` pipeline?

alex: yup. here is the relevant error snippet from the runner:```sops: ERROR: failed to decrypt /workspace/helm/values.sops.yaml: decrypt failed: rpc error: code = PermissionDenied desc = access denied to kms key 'projects/redwood-kms/locations/global/keyRings/kr/cryptoKeys/walrus-eu'```

sam: hmm that key is in global, but our gitops runner in us-west has restricted egress to eu KMS per recent policy. maybe it's trying to use the wrong service account/endpoint.

kavya: +1. We rolled out the KMS egress restrictions last week to block wide egress for runners. Did the runner SA get the kms.decrypter role in that key's IAM policy?

maria: checking IAM now.```gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy walrus-eu --keyring kr --location global --project redwood-kms```

infra-bot: deploy-bot detected failed canary for walrus v3.2.1 — aborting rollout and starting fallback rules.

ryan: note: when the canary failed the autoscaler kicked a fallback to the on-demand gpu pool in us-west to run scheduled batch tests. that pool uses p4d instances — we're incurring ~$11k/day if this keeps running. :grimacing:

alex: ugh. so two separate pain points: 1) SOPS decryption failing due to KMS access/egress, 2) autoscaler fallback consuming expensive GPUs because eu-west nodes didn't come up.

sam: for (1) quick workaround — we can temporarily set `helm.valuesSecret` to the decrypted values as a pipeline variable for the canary only. ugly but fast. For medium fix, ensure runner has kms access or move key to eu-west region key ring.

kavya: prefer not to move keys — compliance prefers global keyring for that app. I'll add runner SA to IAM and put a safe egress exception for the gitops runners to reach KMS. Need approval from security.

maria: security flagged that egress exception already in #eng-security. tagging @security for emergency approval? we may get an exception if we limit to kms endpoint only.

alex: also for (2) the cluster autoscaler logs show failures to schedule because the GPU node template has `node.kubernetes.io/unreachable:NoSchedule` taint applied by cloud-init on boot for our eu-west images. looks like a packaging update caused cloud-init to add a blocking script; nodes never become Ready. logs:```k8s: node walrus-eu-3 NotReady kubelet: failed to start cloud-init: exit status 1```

ryan: oh right, the image baked last night included the new NVLink kernel that requires a later AMI. Our autoscaler keeps spinning until timeout and then falls back to on-demand pool. Fix is to pin to previous AMI or adjust the startup script.

sam: for immediate relief I can patch the walrus HPA/PodDisruptionBudget to avoid triggering the autoscaler fallback and let current on-prem pods handle traffic for a couple hours. low-risk?

kavya: ok go for the IAM & egress exception plan + SAM's quick helm var patch. I'll open a security ticket and mention the narrow KMS endpoint allowlist.

maria: applied temporary helm override to the canary, forcing decrypted values as pipeline secret (will expire in 6 hours). canary started progressing again at 1972105000.

infra-bot: note: walrus canary reached 50% at 1972106000, no new errors.

alex: thank you all. next steps: kavya to track security approval, ryan to revert AMI or roll a fixed image, sam to revert temporary helm override after rollout, and i'll open a cost alert to kill the on-demand gpu nodes if spend crosses $2k/day.

ryan: I'll patch image tomorrow AM and coordinate a controlled AMI rollback now.

sam: will add a postmortem in /docs/incidents/walrus-1972103456 and add a checklist so we don't lose the KMS-to-runner mapping on future policy changes.

alex: one more: please add a small unit in our GitOps pipeline that validates SOPS decrypt using the runner SA before attempting rollout — catch this earlier.

maria: noted. creating a pipeline preflight step ticket.
